name: Short Call Calendar Spread (Reverse Call Calendar)
summary: Buy the near-term call and sell the longer-dated call at the same strike; a net credit structure that wants a large move or a collapse in back-month vol, and that goes naked after the front leg expires.
max_profit: Limited and approximately equal to the net credit received, achieved when the underlying moves far enough from the strike that both legs converge in value (both deep ITM at parity, or both worthless).
max_loss: UNDEFINED in the general case. Before front expiry the practical worst case is the loss when spot pins the strike at front expiry (the long dies, the short retains value). After front expiry the remaining short back-month call is NAKED with theoretically unlimited loss. This is why the automation must never hold it past the front expiry.
breakevens: Two, bracketing the strike; the position is profitable OUTSIDE the band, roughly strike +/- (1.0 to 1.3) x the credit in underlying points at front expiry.

greeks.gamma: positive near the front expiry (long the near-dated gamma)
greeks.theta: negative, the mirror of a long calendar
greeks.vega: negative (net short vega); this is the primary edge when back-month vol is rich

when_to_use: Only when the term structure is in steep contango: back_IV - front_IV >= 5 vol points AND IV rank > 60, i.e. back months are expensive relative to the front. Also used ahead of an expected regime shift where a big directional move is likely. This is a rare, tactical structure and is dominated by simpler short-vol trades for most accounts.
entry_rules: REQUIRES ALPACA OPTIONS LEVEL 4. A level 3 account CANNOT open this - the short leg is the later-expiring one, so it is uncovered the moment the long front leg expires, and most brokers (Alpaca included) treat the whole structure as an uncovered short call at entry. Included here for completeness; the automation must reject it while the account is level 3.
back_IV - front_IV >= 5.0 vol points AND IV rank > 60.
Credit received >= 20% of the back-month option's premium; otherwise the reward does not justify the tail.
Size by naked-short margin, not by credit: assume 20% of notional per contract.
Never on a name with binary event risk inside the back-month window.
management_rules: Profit target: close at +50% of the credit received.
Stop: close at -100% of the credit received (loss equal to the credit).
Vol stop: close if back-month IV rises 5 vol points above entry.
Never allow the front (long) leg to expire while the back (short) leg is open - that converts the trade into a naked short call.
Position cap: at most 1 unit, and only if the account is level 4; otherwise zero.
exit_rules: Close the ENTIRE structure no later than 5 trading days before the FRONT (long) leg expires. This is the defining rule - the protection expires first.
If the short back-month call goes ITM with |delta| >= 0.85, close the short leg immediately regardless of the calendar.
Close the short call before ex-dividend whenever its extrinsic value < the dividend per share.
When legging out, buy back the SHORT leg first, then sell the long.
If the account is level 3, the only valid action is to reject the trade at entry.
assignment_risk: Severe and structurally worse than any long calendar: the SHORT leg is the long-dated one, so assignment risk persists for months and is not extinguished by the front leg. Assignment on a short call delivers -100 shares; once the front long call has expired there is no cover at all. Dividend-driven early assignment applies at every ex-date in the back-month window.
buying_power: Naked short call margin: the greater of 20% of underlying value minus OTM amount, or 10% of underlying value, plus the option premium; per contract this is typically $2,000-$8,000 on a $100-$400 underlying. Alpaca reserves this for the life of the trade.
liquidity_needs: Both months OI >= 500, back-month spread <= $0.20. Because exits are forced by risk rather than by profit, execution quality matters more than in the long version.
common_mistakes: Believing the risk is defined - it is not; letting the front leg expire and waking up naked short; using it as a cheap way to be 'long volatility' when it is actually short vega; running it on a dividend payer and getting called away the night before ex-date.
zero_dte_notes: Never. A 0DTE long leg against a longer short leg means you are naked short by the closing bell today.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
